questions.title: Number object properties and methods
questions.prompt:
Write a function `describe(value)` that returns:

- `"not a number"` if `Number.isNaN(value)`
- `"infinite"` if the value isn't finite (`Number.isFinite()`)
- `"integer"` if `Number.isInteger(value)`
- otherwise the value rounded to 2 decimals with `toFixed()`
hints: Check the cases in the order listed.

questions.title: The Math object
questions.prompt: Write `hypotenuse(a, b)` that returns √(a² + b²) rounded to **2 decimal places** as a number, using `Math.sqrt()`, `Math.pow()` (or `**`) and `Math.round()`.

questions.title: Random number in a range
questions.prompt: Write `getRandomInt(min, max)` that returns a random **whole number** from `min` to `max`, **inclusive**, with every value equally likely.
questions.solution: const getRandomInt = (min, max) => Math.floor(Math.random() * (max - min + 1)) + min;

tests.name: Always an integer within 5..8
tests.code:
for (let i = 0; i < 3000; i++) { const n = getRandomInt(5, 8); if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 5 || n > 8) return false; }
return true;

tests.name: Every value 5..8 appears

questions.title: PIG: score a turn
questions.prompt:
In the chapter's PIG game, a player rolls a die until they decide to stop or roll a **1**. Rolling a 1 ends the turn and **loses** all points from that turn.

Write `scoreTurn(rolls)`, where `rolls` is the array of rolls in a turn. Return the sum of the rolls, or 0 if any roll is a 1 (stop reading at the 1).
hints: Loop through the rolls; if a roll is 1, return 0; otherwise add it.

questions.title: Capitalize words
questions.prompt:
Write `capitalizeWords(text)` that returns the text with the first letter of each word uppercase and the rest lowercase. Words are separated by single spaces.

```
capitalizeWords("hello WORLD from js")   // "Hello World From Js"
```
hints: split(" "), change each word with charAt(0).toUpperCase() + slice(1).toLowerCase(), then join(" ").

tests.name: "hello WORLD from js"
tests.code: return capitalizeWords("hello WORLD from js") === "Hello World From Js";

questions.title: Palindromes
questions.prompt:
Write `isPalindrome(text)` that returns `true` if the text reads the same backwards, **ignoring case and anything that isn't a letter or digit**.

```
isPalindrome("Never odd or even")   // true
isPalindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!")   // true
isPalindrome("JavaScript")   // false
```
hints: Build a cleaned string: lowercase it and keep only characters where /[a-z0-9]/ matches.

tests.name: "Never odd or even" is a palindrome
tests.code: return isPalindrome("Never odd or even") === true;

tests.name: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!" is a palindrome
tests.code: return isPalindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!") === true;

questions.title: Mask a card number
questions.prompt:
Write `maskCard(number)` that takes a card number **string** (spaces and dashes allowed) and returns only the digits, with every digit except the **last four** replaced by `*`.

```
maskCard("1234-5678-9012-3456")   // "************3456"
```
hints: Remove non-digits with replace(/\D/g, "") or a loop.
slice(-4) gets the last four; padStart() can add the stars.

questions.title: Create an array from a string
questions.prompt: Write `countWords(text)` that returns the number of words in the text. Words are separated by one or more spaces, and leading/trailing spaces don't count. An empty or all-space string has 0 words.
hints: trim() first. Then split(" ") and ignore empty strings — or split on a regular expression /\s+/.

tests.name: "  the quick   brown fox " has 4 words
tests.code: return countWords("  the quick   brown fox ") === 4;

questions.title: Count Down: days until a date
questions.prompt:
Like the chapter's Count Down application, write `daysUntil(target, from)` that returns the number of **whole days** from the Date `from` to the Date `target` (round **up** partial days). If the target has passed, return 0.

```
daysUntil(new Date(2026, 11, 25), new Date(2026, 11, 1))   // 24
```
hints: Subtracting two Dates gives milliseconds. One day is 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 ms.

questions.title: Dates and the Internationalization API
questions.prompt:
Write two functions:

1. `addDays(date, days)` returns a **new** Date that many days later, without changing `date`.
2. `formatLong(date)` returns the date formatted with the **Internationalization API** for `en-US` with the weekday, month name, day and year:

```
formatLong(new Date(2026, 11, 25))   // "Friday, December 25, 2026"
```
hints: const copy = new Date(date); copy.setDate(copy.getDate() + days);
new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { weekday: "long", month: "long", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" }).format(date)

tests.name: addDays crosses a month
tests.code:
const d = addDays(new Date(2026, 0, 30), 5);
return d.getMonth() === 1 && d.getDate() === 4;

tests.name: addDays does not change the original
